clinician.trajectory_summary: A male infant presented with multiple severe congenital anomalies detected prenatally, including microcephaly, CNS infarcts, polymicrogyria, VSD, and narrowed aortic arch. Postnatally, the infant exhibited respiratory distress, subclinical seizures, and further cardiac abnormalities (fenestrated atrial septum, hypoplastic left ventricle and aortic arch, PDA). Extensive imaging confirmed these CNS and cardiac findings. Genetic testing via XomeDxXpress Clinical Exome Sequence Analysis identified a de novo heterozygous variant at c. 2771 G>A of the Col4a1 gene, confirming the diagnosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Prenatal ultrasound showed multiple fetal anomalies including microcephaly, multifocal hemorrhagic/ischemic infarcts, ex-vacuo dilatation, polymicrogyria, VSD, and narrowed aortic arch.
Fetal MRI of the brain confirmed suspected ultrasound findings of CNS anomalies.

Postnatal echocardiography showed fenestrated atrial septum, moderate mid-muscular VSD, mild to moderate hypoplastic left ventricle, moderately hypoplastic left aortic arch, small to moderate patent ductus arteriosus, and suprasystemic right ventricular systolic pressure.

Postnatal MRI of the brain confirmed multifocal infarcts, diffuse mild polymicrogyria, dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, optic nerve hypoplasia, a defect within the intraventricular septum, and inferior vermian hypoplasia.
XomeDxXpress Clinical Exome Sequence Analysis identified a de novo heterozygous variant at c. 2771 G>A of the Col4a1 gene.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The identification of a specific de novo pathogenic variant in COL4A1 gene provides a definitive genetic diagnosis, making other genetic etiologies less likely as the primary cause of the observed phenotype.

remaining_uncertainties: Detailed clinical course and management post-diagnosis were not explicitly documented.
Family history regarding similar conditions or genetic disorders was not reported.
